## Main deck sections (slides 1–15)

## Slide 1 — Cover

- Title: TravelTrust  
- **On-slide taglines (three lines, match `SLIDES_EN`)**: (1) Trip-order fintech; (2) Custody · fulfillment · disputes on one path; (3) Disclosures follow releases + Whitepaper. Definition + figures boundary still anchor on **slide 2**.

## Slide 2 — TravelTrust (definition + boundary)

**On slide**: **two lines**—definition + boundary (principal vs recurring revenue; figures under Whitepaper + NDA). **Positioning** (no “flip incumbents overnight”) stays in **speaker notes** only—see `SLIDES_EN`.

## Slide 3 — Pain

1. Facts don’t line up  
2. Disputes drag  
3. Traveler vs platform order funds—who may release, unclear?  

**On slide (one line after pains)**: **Clip nails the first two; the third is the table line.**

## Slide 4 — Trip-order: align delivery and disputes · fulfillment loop (vector loop)

One connected loop from browse to pay; **vector loop + bottom caption** on slide. Order: find → book → align delivery → resolve issues → follow published disclosures (short node label on figure: “Published disclosures”; same sequence as `SLIDES_EN` speaker bullets). **Chrome title** stresses fulfillment loop, not fee unpack on this slide.

## Slide 5 — Protocol stack · order rules | responsibility slices (stack)

Same single-trip logic as slide 4, **vertical** five-step stack; **title** re-anchors responsibility slices / control plane; no undisclosed metrics on slide.

## Slide 6 — Why now (evidence-style, qualitative)

- **Demand** (`06` §2.4): fulfillment certainty matters → **auditable rules** fit institutional risk models.  
- **Supply** (same): portable reputation + **clear release rules**.  
- **Regulatory** (same): disclosure + fund-path scrutiny → **principal vs protocol-fee separation** (not legal advice).  
- **Window** (same closing): fragmented distribution → **embeddable** custody/dispute becomes channel infra; delay shifts **who templates first** (not a subscription nudge).  
- **Evidence**: comps/metrics under **NDA**; **no** unaudited public TAM absolutes.

## Slide 7 — Three lines to remember (three bullets, one slide)

**Fees & take are ours; trip money isn’t.**  
**TTG: votes only—not paying for trips.**  
**Disclosure cadence: published releases + version/env labels (details: Whitepaper).**

## Slide 8 — One order: delivery aligned?

**On slide**: two thesis lines plus a short **materials / 45·55 verbal discipline** line (see `SLIDES_EN`).

## Slide 9 — System strengths

**On slide**: **single-row pillars** (fulfillment · order alignment · … · published releases/labels). **Summary** (UX + embeddable rails) lives in **speaker notes** only—matches `SLIDES_EN`.

## Slide 10 — Published path · disclosure boundary (outer-ring disclosure | FeeRouter)

On slide: **Disclosure + 100% (Whitepaper) + 45% / 55%** structure only; **chrome title** re-anchors disclosure boundary (FeeRouter token retained for machine build); **gas / arbitration / slashing** are **orthogonal** denominators—voice track must match [06-Whitepaper.md](../06-Whitepaper.md) **§06**.

## Slide 11 — Roadmap & timing (qualitative)

- **Today**: demonstrable main chain (market→orders→fulfillment→disputes/ratings→reputation→community). **No** blanket “fully live” unless formally announced.  
- **Four tracks** (aligned to on-slide pills)  
  - **Product**: loop quality, fulfillment tooling, stability, regional UX pilots  
  - **On-chain**: roll out by country/environment—published releases + environment labels  
  - **Market**: channel pilots aligned to disclosure cadence  
  - **Compliance & ops cadence**: quarterly metrics under **NDA**  
- **Horizon**: public slides **are not** performance commitments or substitutes for signed agreements.

## Slide 12 — Go-to-market (institutional summary)

- **Supply**: provider agreements and KYB/KYC where required, SKU + Escrow milestone alignment, fulfillment training, support handoff.  
- **Demand**: destination content matrix, social matrix, community/ambassador programs (**no** manipulation or investment advice).  
- **KOLs & channels**: disclosed deals; attribution; fee **accounting** separate from protocol narrative where applicable; OTA/DMC pilots by region.  
- **Operating loop**: product—protocol—market—compliance feedback; public quotes only from **pre-cleared** materials.  
- **Reminder**: qualitative here; **targets and rev-shares** live under NDA/IR worksheets.

## Slide 13 — Competitive matrix (qualitative)

- **Web2 OTA**: matching/inventory strength; weaker **auditable disputes** and **portable reputation**.  
- **Crypto rails**: payment finality; rarely a **travel fulfillment state machine / stack**.  
- **TravelTrust**: fulfillment evidence + escrow ritual + integrated stack; TTG **not** default travel payment; public fee layer **100%/45%/55%** (`06` §6).  
- **Footnote (on slide)**: follow the published Whitepaper; line-item tables in the NDA room—**not** informal drafting-only wording.
- **Partner-meeting depth (IR memo)**: FAQ items **28–31** align with IC notes and this slide’s matrix footnotes; the shipped **03-FAQ PDF** uses institutional wording (no LP-facing deep-dive / item-chain navigation). On-slide matrix footnotes remain **15** pages.

## Slide 14 — Narrative journey (teaching case, anonymized)

- **Discover/Match**: traveler **Alex**, guide **Sam** (pseudonyms)—milestones and quote.  
- **Escrow**: funded; state “in fulfillment” (allowlisted stables, etc.).  
- **Fulfillment**: proofs; **no dispute** → release + positive reputation.  
- **Dispute path**: resolver decision; **arbitration economics ≠ FeeRouter 45%/55% denominator**—always footnote.  
- **Reputation/community**: outcomes on record; **cross-channel reuse** story (not a performance claim).

## Slide 15 — Asks & next conversation (close + public DD rails)

- **Asks**: trust · fulfillment · ecosystem (on slide).  
- **Disclosure & cadence**: published releases **and environment labels** (same as `SLIDES_EN` closing slide).  
- **Next**: platform vs rails in parallel; quant + legal text after NDA.  
- **After the meeting**: FAQ → Whitepaper (**don’t verbally mash 45/55 with gas/slashing**).  
- **Public DD excerpts** (expand in notes): OTA vs infra—**both** embeddable custody/dispute. **TTG vs order cash—separate**. Deployment proof via released addresses + environment labels (detail **NDA**). Full Q&A: [03-FAQ.md](../03-FAQ.md).

## Design guardrails

1. No subscription-style CTAs on landing.  
2. Do not claim live production domains without **published** announcements and matching **environment labels**.  
3. Keep governance, returns, allocations, and corporate equity in separate lanes.  
4. Preserve the order–escrow–dispute spine.

Pair with [01-OnePager.md](01-OnePager.md) and [03-FAQ.md](03-FAQ.md).
